summary: Deployed a demo app on node2:8080 (systemd service app8080.service) reachable from node3 only via a WireGuard tunnel terminated on node1 (VyOS). node1 runs wg0 (10.200.0.1/24, UDP 51820, peer node3), forwards+masquerades tunnel traffic to node2:8080 via an ipv4 forward-filter default-drop ruleset, and node2's firewalld default-deny zone only accepts port 8080 from node1's LAN IP (10.100.226.10) via a rich rule — so node3 cannot reach node2:8080 directly, only through the tunnel. Verified with curl end-to-end, and confirmed a specific route (10.100.226.11 via wg0) on node3 forces all such traffic through the tunnel. Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time reboot protocol on all three nodes, capturing baseline, restart ack, changed boot_id, and post-recovery health/functional proof for each. Along the way fixed a pre-existing app8080.service unit dependency (network-online.target) that would have hung indefinitely on node2 due to an unrelated second NIC (enp8s0) with no DHCP lease.
actions_performed: Surveyed node1 (VyOS), node2 (RHEL9), node3 (RHEL9) network/OS state
Deployed Python HTTP app on node2:8080 as systemd service app8080.service, enabled+started
Generated WireGuard keypairs on node1 (via VyOS PKI helper) and node3 (wg genkey/pubkey)
Configured VyOS wg0 interface, peer, firewall input/forward filters (default-drop with explicit allows), and source NAT masquerade rule on node1; committed and saved
Configured wg-quick@wg0 client on node3 with AllowedIPs scoped to node2's IP only, enabled as systemd service
Added firewalld rich rule on node2 permitting TCP 8080 only from node1's IP, confirmed default zone otherwise rejects
Verified end-to-end curl from node3 to node2:8080 works only via the tunnel and route table forces path through wg0
Captured pre-restart boot_id and health baseline for all 3 nodes
Rebooted node1, node2, node3 sequentially (one at a time), polled each until exec available again, confirmed changed boot_id each time
Fixed app8080.service unit (After=network.target instead of network-online.target) after discovering it hung on node2 boot due to an unrelated second NIC without DHCP
Re-verified WireGuard handshake, NAT/firewall counters, firewalld rule persistence, and end-to-end app reachability after each reboot

evidence.requirement: WireGuard tunnel terminated on node1, client on node3
evidence.summary: Keys generated on both ends, wg0 configured and committed on VyOS node1, wg-quick@wg0 active on node3 with successful handshake

evidence.requirement: node3 reaches node2:8080 only through the WireGuard-gated path
evidence.summary: VyOS default-drop forward filter + wg0-scoped accept rule + source NAT masquerade, plus node2 firewalld rich rule restricted to node1's IP; curl from node3 succeeded and forward-filter rule 10 hit counter incremented, proving traffic transited the tunnel and NAT
